description: The push west — Lewis and Clark's overland expedition, fur-trade outposts like Astoria, Texas independence, and the Oregon Trail migrations that reshaped the continent.

events.title: Camp Dubois established
events.desc: The Corps of Discovery gathered and trained through the winter at a camp on the Illinois side of the Mississippi, across from the mouth of the Missouri River.

events.title: Expedition departs St. Louis
events.desc: Meriwether Lewis and William Clark led roughly forty men up the Missouri River, beginning a journey to explore the newly acquired Louisiana Territory.

events.title: Council with the Otoe and Missouria
events.desc: Near present-day Council Bluffs, the expedition held its first formal meeting with Native leaders, delivering peace medals and messages from President Jefferson.

events.title: Death of Sergeant Charles Floyd
events.desc: Floyd died of what was likely a ruptured appendix, becoming the expedition's only fatality; he was buried on a bluff near modern Sioux City.

events.title: Standoff with the Teton Sioux
events.desc: A tense confrontation over trade and passage nearly turned violent near present-day Pierre before both sides backed down.

events.title: Fort Mandan built for winter
events.desc: The expedition wintered among the Mandan and Hidatsa villages in present-day North Dakota, trading and gathering crucial geographic knowledge of the route ahead.

events.title: Sacagawea joins the expedition
events.desc: The Shoshone teenager and her husband, fur trader Toussaint Charbonneau, were hired as interpreters at Fort Mandan; she gave birth to a son there that winter.

events.title: Expedition resumes westward
events.desc: With winter over, the Corps left Fort Mandan in smaller boats, pushing further up the Missouri than any prior American expedition.

events.title: Portage around the Great Falls
events.desc: The party spent nearly a month hauling boats and supplies overland around a series of five waterfalls on the Missouri River in present-day Montana.

events.title: Meeting the Shoshone at Lemhi Pass
events.desc: Crossing the Continental Divide, the party met a Shoshone band whose chief turned out to be Sacagawea's brother, securing horses essential for the mountain crossing.

events.title: Crossing the Bitterroot Mountains
events.desc: A grueling, near-starvation trek over the Lolo Trail proved the hardest stretch of the journey, aided afterward by the Nez Perce.

events.title: First sight of the Pacific Ocean
events.desc: Following the Snake and Columbia Rivers, the expedition reached tidewater near the mouth of the Columbia, confirming an overland route to the Pacific.

events.title: Fort Clatsop built for winter
events.desc: The Corps built a small log fort near present-day Astoria, Oregon, and spent a damp, difficult winter there before starting the journey home.

events.title: The party splits to explore more territory
events.desc: On the return trip, Lewis and Clark divided their group near present-day Missoula, Montana, to explore the Marias and Yellowstone Rivers separately.

events.title: Skirmish with Blackfeet warriors
events.desc: Lewis's party clashed with a group of young Blackfeet men over horses and weapons, the expedition's only violent encounter with Native people, leaving two men dead.

events.title: Reunion at the Yellowstone confluence
events.desc: The two divided parties rejoined where the Yellowstone River meets the Missouri, in present-day North Dakota, before heading downriver together.

events.title: Return to St. Louis
events.desc: The Corps of Discovery arrived back in St. Louis after more than two years, having traveled roughly eight thousand miles and mapped a route to the Pacific.

events.title: Pacific Fur Company founded
events.desc: New York merchant John Jacob Astor formed a company to compete in the Pacific fur trade, sending one party by sea and another overland toward the mouth of the Columbia River.

events.title: Fort Astoria founded
events.desc: Astor's Pacific Fur Company established a trading post at the mouth of the Columbia River, the first American-owned settlement on the Pacific coast.

events.title: Robert Stuart finds South Pass
events.desc: Returning overland from Astoria toward St. Louis, Robert Stuart's party crossed the Rockies through a low, wagon-friendly gap that later became the key gateway of the Oregon Trail.

events.title: Fort Astoria sold to the British
events.desc: With war underway and a British warship reportedly approaching, Astor's partners sold the fort to the rival North West Company; it was renamed Fort George.

events.title: Battle of San Jacinto
events.desc: Sam Houston led the Texian army in a swift, decisive rout of Santa Anna's forces near present-day Houston, securing Texas independence in less than twenty minutes of fighting.

events.title: Sam Houston inaugurated as Texas president
events.desc: Sam Houston took office as the first elected president of the newly declared Republic of Texas at its temporary capital in Columbia.

events.title: Texas annexed by the United States
events.desc: After years of debate over slavery and expansion, Congress voted to annex the Republic of Texas as the 28th state, a cause Sam Houston had long championed.

events.title: Joe Meek at the Green River rendezvous
events.desc: Mountain man Joe Meek trapped for years with the Rocky Mountain Fur Company, gathering each summer with trappers and Native traders at rendezvous like this one in present-day Wyoming.

events.title: The Great Migration sets out on the Oregon Trail
events.desc: Roughly a thousand settlers, including former mountain man Joe Meek, left Missouri for Oregon Country in the largest wagon migration the trail had yet seen.

events.title: Champoeg vote for a provisional government
events.desc: Settlers meeting at Champoeg narrowly voted to organize a provisional government for Oregon Country, with Joe Meek among the leading voices pushing the measure through.

events.title: Joe Meek becomes US Marshal of Oregon
events.desc: After traveling to Washington to lobby Congress for federal protection of Oregon settlers, Meek returned as the new territory's first appointed US marshal.
